question: Should OpenClaw permanently require injected WhatsApp media readers to provide explicit local roots and publish the focused base64/transcoding SDK APIs as the supported plugin contract?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility and security-boundary decision, not a mechanical defect: preserving the old implicit reader behavior would weaken the stated boundary, while accepting the branch creates a permanent SDK surface.

options.title: Accept the canonical boundary
options.body: Approve the explicit-root requirement and focused SDK exports, then merge after normal required checks complete.

options.title: Preserve legacy reader behavior
options.body: Require a separately designed, explicitly scoped compatibility path for existing injected readers before merging.

options.title: Pause API expansion
options.body: Keep the WhatsApp refactor open only after splitting or deferring the new public SDK contract for owner discussion.

recommendation.title: Accept the canonical boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the explicit-root requirement and focused SDK exports, then merge after normal required checks complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the repository-member author of the current migration series and can provide the implementation and compatibility context for the owner decision.
